# Build a Free HR Payroll System with Selfie Attendance & GPS | Claude Code + Google Sheets (Mohammad Rameez Imdad, 13.8 min)

**What it is:** a genuine build-and-deploy walkthrough — VS Code + the Claude Code extension writes the actual Apps Script backend and HTML frontend from a queue of 5 prompts, then the presenter deploys the Apps Script backend and hosts the frontend separately on Netlify. 2026-era video.
**Substance:** the strongest video in the batch for our purposes: it is the only one that shows the real AI-build workflow (prompting, generated files, deployment, a real error and its fix) end to end, matching this course's exact target architecture (Apps Script backend + separately hosted frontend for camera/GPS features).

## Ideas, in the video's order
- [0:01:38] Claude Code is installed as a VS Code extension; the presenter opens a **local empty folder** first, then works inside VS Code, not inside the Apps Script editor — the AI writes files on disk (`code.js`, `index.html`), which only later get copied into Apps Script.
- [0:02:11] **The build is deliberately split into 5 separate prompts, queued one after another** ("we have divided this web application in five different prompts... once it's completed prompt one, it will move to prompt two") rather than one giant prompt — a directly reusable habit: break a big app into a short sequence of small, ordered asks instead of one mega-prompt (matches CONTEXT.md's "small asks" guidance almost exactly).
- [0:03:50] After Claude Code finishes, the presenter manually creates a brand-new Sheet (`sheet.new`), opens Extensions → Apps Script, and **pastes the AI-generated `code.js` into the Apps Script editor by hand** — the AI does not deploy anything itself; a human copy-paste bridges local AI output to the live backend.
- [0:04:24] Real deploy sequence, matching other videos: Deploy → New deployment → Web app → access "Anyone" → Deploy → **Authorize access → Advanced → go to (unsafe) project → allow all requested scopes** — this "unverified app" warning screen is shown and clicked through, a good real screenshot for explaining OAuth consent to kids.
- [0:04:57] The resulting `.../exec` URL is copied back into VS Code, into `index.html`, replacing a `const API_...` placeholder — the concrete mechanic of "wire the frontend to the backend" that the course's Netlify-frontend plan depends on.
- [0:05:29]-[0:06:35] **Netlify deploy by drag-and-drop**: create/log into a Netlify account, "browse files to upload," select the `index.html`, wait for upload, rename the project — the frontend now lives on a totally separate domain from the Apps Script backend.
- **[0:06:35]-[0:07:41] A real, filmable AI-adjacent failure and its fix:** first login attempt on the freshly deployed site fails ("it will give us the error because we don't have set up the demo data... it will not allow you to login") — not an AI hallucination, but a very real "forgot a setup step" bug. Fix: go back to the Apps Script editor, select the `setupDemoData` function from the dropdown, click Run — after that, login works. This is exactly the class of bug CONTEXT.md asks us to log (a broken app and its concrete recovery step), even though the cause is a missing initialization step rather than the AI rewriting code.
- [0:08:13] Project sites store **latitude/longitude and an "attendance radius"** (e.g. 200 m) — geofencing is done by comparing the employee's reported GPS position against a stored site location, a real, understandable geofencing pattern.
- [0:11:28]-[0:12:34] **Selfie check-in**: the browser asks for camera permission, captures a photo, and — critically — the presenter narrates that processing "takes some time... 3 to 5 seconds... because it is using the doPost function... the image will be saved in your Google Drive and the data will be saved in your Google Sheets" — a rare, explicit, correct explanation of `doPost`, async latency, and where an uploaded image actually ends up (Drive, not the Sheet itself).
- Camera and GPS both work here because the **frontend is hosted on Netlify, not inside the Apps Script HtmlService iframe** — this directly confirms CONTEXT.md's assumption that camera/mic are blocked inside Apps Script's sandboxed iframe and that moving the frontend off-platform is the real fix, demonstrated in practice rather than just asserted.

## What the frames add
Frames are unusually rich here: [0:01:30]-[0:02:30] show the actual VS Code + Claude Code chat panel with the queued prompts and a visible "Foundation — Apps Script backend, login, sidebar shell, custom popup" prompt text on screen — a real example of how one prompt in the sequence is scoped. [0:04:10]-[0:04:30] show the literal "New deployment" dialog and the "Google hasn't verified this app" warning screen. [0:05:20]-[0:06:00] show the Netlify upload flow (drag-and-drop target, "Push your ideas to the web" homepage, file browser, project rename). [0:07:20]-[0:07:50] show the live "Attendance System Login... Authenticating..." screen before and after the fix. [0:12:00]-[0:12:30] show the actual selfie-capture modal with a live camera preview and a "Processing attendance..." spinner.

## For our class (14-15, Gemini writes the code, Apps Script + Sheets)
### Backend concepts it shows or explains
Splitting a build into an ordered sequence of small prompts; the human-copy-paste bridge between AI-generated code and the live Apps Script project; the full OAuth-consent deploy flow; geofencing by comparing GPS coordinates against a stored radius; `doPost` + async processing delay + where uploaded files actually land (Drive vs Sheet); moving the frontend off Apps Script (to Netlify) specifically to unlock camera/GPS.

### Becomes something kids do (activity, mini-project, milestone), concrete enough to run next week
This is close to a template for the course's own final-project pattern: (1) build a small Apps Script backend with Gemini, in a handful of small prompts; (2) deploy it and copy the `.../exec` URL; (3) build a tiny separate HTML page (hosted on Netlify or similar) that `fetch()`es that URL; (4) only then add a camera-based feature (e.g. "upload a photo of your homework" instead of selfie check-in) and watch it work where it wouldn't inside Apps Script alone.

### Traps a kid will hit
Forgetting a one-time setup/seed step after deploying (exactly what happened here) is highly likely to happen to a 14-year-old too — worth pre-teaching as "if login or the first screen fails right after deploying, check whether you skipped a setup function" as a first debugging instinct, since this video shows the fix takes seconds once you know to look there. Also: the OAuth "unverified app" warning screen is exactly what a kid's own Gemini-built project will show on first deploy, so it should be pre-explained, not just clicked through blindly as this video does.

### Doesn't transfer, and why
Claude Code as a paid VS Code extension is a different tool from Gemini directly in the browser (the course's actual setup) — the specific queued-prompt UI won't exist for the class, but the underlying habit (small sequential prompts, human bridges AI output to deployment) transfers directly regardless of tool.

## Honest caveats
The video is still a smooth, edited demo — the "forgot demo data" bug is the only real failure shown; no messier failures (AI rewriting working code, a broken deploy, a quota error) appear. Treat this as the best-case version of the workflow the course wants, not proof it always goes this cleanly.
